en.title: DCU's Clayface Movie Merges Two Iconic Villains for 2026
en.summary: A brand new DC Universe film centered on the shapeshifting villain Clayface is officially slated for a 2026 release. This upcoming movie is set to combine elements from two distinct comic book iterations of the character, offering a fresh take on the classic Batman foe.
en.body:
The world of DC Comics is no stranger to iconic villains, and the shapeshifting terror known as Clayface is no exception. While fans eagerly await the full reveal of the DC Universe's new Batman, the eerie **Clayface** is already set to make a significant splash. A live-action film titled **Clayface** has been officially greenlit for a 2026 release as part of the DCU's **Chapter One: Gods and Monsters** slate, with Warner Bros. Pictures set to distribute it on October 23, 2026. This project, developed under the guidance of **James Gunn** and **Peter Safran**, promises a unique interpretation of the character.

The upcoming **Clayface** movie is poised to be a fascinating blend, merging two different comic book versions of the villain into a single, cohesive character. This approach acknowledges the rich history of the character while streamlining it for a modern cinematic universe. The original iteration, appearing in the Golden Age of comics, was **Matt Hagen**, a former actor who turned to crime. However, the film also draws inspiration from **Sondra Fuller**, also known as **Lady Clay**, an agent of the nefarious Kobra organization who gained her shapeshifting abilities through experimental surgery. The decision to combine these distinct origins suggests a narrative that will explore the multifaceted nature of **Clayface**, potentially delving into themes of identity, ambition, and transformation.

## A Legacy of Shapeshifting Villains

Over the decades, **Clayface** has manifested in various forms, each with their own backstory and motivations. The character's malleable nature has allowed writers to explore different facets of villainy, from simple greed to profound psychological turmoil. The **DCU**'s choice to fuse **Matt Hagen** and **Sondra Fuller** indicates a desire to create a singular, compelling antagonist that encapsulates the essence of **Clayface**'s threat. While the film does not currently plan to introduce the **DCU**'s incarnation of **Batman**, the focus remains squarely on the villain's origins and capabilities. This allows for a deep dive into a character often overshadowed by the Caped Crusader, giving **Clayface** the spotlight he deserves.

## What This Means for DCU Fans

For dedicated **DC Comics** fans, this announcement is a thrilling development. The potential to see a character with such a complex and varied history brought to life in the new **DCU** is immense. The merging of two distinct **Clayface** personas could lead to a more nuanced and unpredictable villain, one whose powers and motivations are deeply intertwined. It also suggests that **DC Studios** is willing to explore less mainstream, yet highly compelling, characters as the foundation of its new cinematic universe. The anticipation is palpable, as fans speculate on how these combined origins will translate to the screen and what kind of impact this **Clayface** will have on the nascent **Gods and Monsters** chapter.

## What's Next

The **Clayface** film is slated for release on October 23, 2026, as part of the **DCU**'s **Chapter One: Gods and Monsters**. Further details regarding casting, the director, and the specific narrative approach are expected to be revealed as development progresses.

content_raw: Matt Hagen may be the titular Clayface of the newest DC Universe movie, but the Batman villain has had several alter egos throughout his comics tenure.
